question:
A 15-year-old male presents for evaluation with symptoms including irritability, weight loss of 1.8 kg,
diarrhea, and sleep disturbance. He denies any social stressors or changes. Physical examination
reveals a tired-appearing patient with temperature 37.1°C, heart rate 100/min, respiratory rate 19/min,
and blood pressure 144/99 mm Hg. His skin is moist, and he has normal pupils and extraocular
movements without thyroid eye disease. His thyroid is palpable but nontender, without bruit. Reflexes
are brisk bilaterally, and there is no proptosis. Laboratory results show: - TSH: 0.1 μU/mL (reference:
0.5–4.0) - Free thyroxine: 5.8 ng/dL (reference: 0.59–2.45) - Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate and
C-reactive protein A thyroid uptake scan demonstrates low radioiodine uptake. Which condition most
likely explains this patient's clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Subacute thyroiditis (B) Thyroid
hormone resistance syndrome (C) Ingestion of a liothyronine supplement (D) Autonomous thyroid
nodule (E) Iodine-induced hyperthyroidism (F) Central hyperthyroidism (G) Hashimoto thyroiditis (H)
Silent thyroiditis (I) Thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma (J) Graves disease
 A. Hashimoto thyroiditis
B. Ingestion of a liothyronine supplement
C. Thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting pituitary adenoma
D. Thyroid hormone resistance syndrome
E. Iodine-induced hyperthyroidism
F. Central hyperthyroidism
G. Autonomous thyroid nodule
H. Silent thyroiditis
I. Graves disease
J. Subacute thyroiditis
